sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (State of Luxembourg; non-decentralized unitary jurisdiction without sub-state tax differentiation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-code tradition with Belgian and French doctrinal influence, extensively harmonized by EU law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) - establishment, services, capital, and payments freedoms (directly effective)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty network (including the BLEU - People's Republic of China BIT of 1984, in force)
Luxembourg - United States DTA (concluded 1996, as amended 2004, 2009, 2011) and the Luxembourg-US FATCA Intergovernmental Agreement
Luxembourg - China DTA (concluded 1991, as amended by Protocol signed 2015)
Luxembourg - United Kingdom DTA (concluded 1967, as amended; continues in force post-Brexit)
Luxembourg - Hong Kong DTA (concluded 2020, in force 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML Law), as amended, and its implementing Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended by the Law of 27 August 2024 (aligning the register with CJEU judgment in Case C-37/20); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Commercial and Companies Register (RCS); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL provisions, Art. 710-1 et seq.); CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF due diligence circulars insofar as payroll/e-money ancillary services touch the financial sector. The global EOR payroll activity is primarily non-financial, but the entity must maintain an AML/CFT compliance file where it qualifies as an 'obliged entity' under Art. 2 of the AML Law via company-service, notarial, or payment-ancillary activities.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (general public view abolished per CJEU C-37/20; access granted to Luxembourg authorities, CSSF, tax administration, financial intelligence unit, credit institutions, and other obliged entities for customer due diligence; third-party access only on demonstrated 'legitimate interest' application to the Luxembourg Business Registers)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts) of the SARL, drafted in French
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic authentic act (no apostille required); executed as a notarial minute before the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal record / certificate of good conduct for each manager, director, and UBO (country of nationality or 10-year residency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal-records authority of the state of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) where the origin state is a Party; consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Hague states; sworn French translation to follow

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each manager, director, and beneficial owner (documents not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the origin country or the issuing state's competent authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / notarial certified-copy certification; accepted by the Luxembourg notary subject to equivalent reliability

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of blocking of the minimum share capital (attestation de blocage de fonds) covering the EUR 12,000 statutory minimum
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution (or EU bank passporting into Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct bank certificate addressed to the notary; no apostille or consular legalization required (bank-origin professional certificate)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales), Title V (Articles 710-1 to 710-27) governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the accounting records; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsman, merchant and tradesman; Luxembourg Labour Code Articles L. 341-1 et seq. where temporary work placement is contemplated.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating under the Ministry of Justice of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; electronic filings accepted through the official portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially authenticated deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif) and Articles of Association (Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS as the official statement of incorporation (déclaration de création d'entreprise).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The standard SARL requires a minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000; the entire nominal capital must be fully subscribed at incorporation, and the cash portion of each share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked (escrow) bank account held at a Luxembourg credit institution and may be released to the company only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report (rapport du réviseur d'entreprises agréé). No proportional capital duty applies; only the fixed registration and publication fees are payable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
The undersigned founding manager(s) of [Company Name], a Luxembourg Société à Responsabilité Limitée, acting pursuant to Article 710-20 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, adopt this First Board Resolution.

1. Share Subscription. The EUR 12,000 share capital is fully subscribed; the statutory paid-up portion is deposited in a blocked bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution (certificate annexed).

2. Registered Office. The registered office is set at [street address], L-[postcode] [city], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

3. Officers. [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) and [Name] Deputy Manager, each authorized, jointly or severally, to complete all incorporation, RCS registration, licensing, and tax filings.

Adopted unanimously, effective upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Share-Capital Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution supervised by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier); the bank's blocked-account certificate is later exhibited to the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders engage a CSSF-licensed Luxembourg bank, complete AML/KYC diligence, and wire at least 25% of the EUR 12,000 subscribed capital to a designated blocked account opened in the name of the future SARL. Obtain the attestation de blocage identifying the company as beneficiary; the account remains frozen until the RCS registration certificate is presented.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founders and intended managers
Bank account opening and KYC/AML forms
Business plan describing the global EOR payroll activity (ISIC 7810)
Power of attorney if the bank is approached through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, supply corroborating source-of-funds evidence; if account opening is refused, a second CSSF-licensed institution may be used without resetting the formation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) in the judicial district of Luxembourg or Diekirch, member of the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary with final draft Statuts compliant with Article 710-2 of the 1915 Law; submit the attested blocked-account certificate; the notary verifies identity, capacity, and absence of manager disqualification, then reads and executes the Acte constitutif. The deed must identify the registered office and name the Gérant(s). The company does not yet possess legal personality at this stage.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national IDs of founders and managers
Registered-office address proof (lease or notarised landlord consent)
Declaration of no criminal disqualification of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or LBR pre-check identifies name conflicts or an invalid corporate object, execute a rectification annex or amend the Statuts before signature; a founder unable to attend may act through a Luxembourg-form power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, official e-filing portal www.lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the executed deed and annexes electronically to the RCS and pays the statutory registration fee online. Upon clearance, the RCS issues an extract and the company acquires legal personality as of the registration date. A certified RCS extract must be retrieved for banking and licensing use.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt for RCS and RESA fees
Paid-up capital attestation from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query for missing annexes or an incompatible statutory object, the notary files a supplementary deed or clarification within five business days; urgent matters may be escalated to the LBR helpdesk.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), 33 rue de Gasperich, L-5826 Hesperange; self-service portal espaces.acd.public.lu and unified platform myGuichet.lu. Indirect taxes: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg; VAT portal espacetva.public.lu. Customs and excise: Administration des Douanes et Accises (ADA), single window myCustoms.lu and Luxembourg Single Window (ICMS). Central business register: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), www.lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL engaged in EOR/staffing: (1) Execute the notarial deed of incorporation and file it with the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via LBR; publish in RESA; obtain the 12-digit RCS matricule number, which is the master company identifier. (2) Before any taxable transaction, file the VAT registration application (Formulaire 640, Module 101 via myGuichet.lu) with AEDT; the VAT identification number (TVA ID) is generally issued within 2-3 weeks. (3) The ACD automatically opens a direct tax file and assigns a fiscal dossier number once RCS registration is notified; all corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT) returns are filed under that number. (4) Obtain the mandatory establishment authorization ('autorisation d'établissement') from the Ministry of the Economy for temporary work agency / staff-leasing activities (classes 78.10-78.20 of the business classification); invoicing payroll services before the authorization is issued is unlawful. (5) Register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) using the GemFlow/Editus platform for social security and payroll withholding accounts. (6) If foreign companies act without a Luxembourg subsidiary (e.g., a foreign EOR entity carrying on activities through a Luxembourg deemed establishment), the non-resident company must file a branch registration with RCS, obtain an EORI number from ADA for goods movements, and appoint an accredited Luxembourg VAT representative when no fixed establishment exists. Deadlines are strict: VAT registration precedes first taxable supply; a foreign enterprise that becomes liable must register within 15 days of exceeding the taxable threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is per se a resident corporate taxpayer, not eligible for pass-through treatment. It is subject to (i) corporate income tax at 17.00% plus the 7% solidarity surcharge (effective 18.19%); (ii) municipal business tax at the communal rate applicable to Luxembourg City of 6.75%, giving an aggregate headline CIT+MBT rate of approximately 24.94%; and (iii) net wealth tax at 0.50% on net taxable assets with a EUR 500,000 exemption and minimum annual NWT of EUR 535 for certain holding/finance entities. Territorial scope: resident SARLs are taxed on worldwide income, with treaty relief, unilateral foreign-tax credit, and participation exemption applying; foreign branch income is typically exempt if subject to taxation in the source country. No tax-exempt zone applies to the SARL; the Luxembourg Freeport is only a customs warehouse facility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election; a SARL is a hardwired corporation. Available elections relevant to an EOR platform: (i) VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') under Article 60 of the VAT Law, allowing the SARL and its Luxembourg affiliates (with financial, economic, and organizational links) to file as a single taxable person; (ii) fiscal unity (tax consolidation) for CIT and MBT under Article 164bis LIR, requiring a 95% direct or indirect holding and a 5-year duration undertaking; (iii) participation exemption election for dividends under Section 166 LIR and capital gains under Section 166bis LIR where the SARL holds at least 10% (or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost) of a qualifying subsidiary for 12 consecutive months and either the subsidiary is subject to an equivalent tax or the SARL is itself a fully taxable resident company; (iv) VAT small-enterprise franchise election for turnover below EUR 35,000, incompatible with invoicing VAT to business clients; and (v) ATAD hybrid mismatch documentation elections pursuant to Sections 62-68 LIR requiring annual documentation of any deductible payments that could be treated as deductible in the recipient state. All elections are exercised in the annual CIT/VAT returns and require advance written documentation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC through the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover in Luxembourg (small-enterprise franchise exemption, Article 57 of the VAT Law). The threshold applies to all taxable supplies of goods and services by an enterprise established in Luxembourg; once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 in a rolling 12-month period, VAT registration becomes mandatory from the first euro. A separate EUR 35,000 ceiling applies to intra-Community acquisitions (Article 58) and to domestic distance sales; the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies to cross-border B2C telecommunications, broadcasting, and digital services. For an EOR platform, payroll service fees are generally taxable supplies; salary and social-security pass-through amounts may be excluded from the VAT base when properly documented as disbursements, which affects whether the EUR 35,000 threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no SAF-T e-audit file, no API-based validation, and no digital stamping requirement. Invoices may be issued on paper, in PDF, or as structured e-invoices, provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are ensured (Articles 74-75 of the VAT Law; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 August 2011). E-invoices conforming to the European standard EN 16931 and exchanged via the Peppol network are accepted and are being increasingly used in B2B cross-border payroll transactions. Invoices must be archived for 10 years. Under the VAT-in-the-Digital-Age (ViDA) agreement reached by ECOFIN in December 2025, an EU-wide e-invoicing obligation for cross-border B2B supplies is to be phased in from 1 July 2030, with Luxembourg expected to transpose the directive and require structured e-invoices; the SARL should therefore build EN 16931/UBL-compliant e-invoicing capability now.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% with credit for input VAT) is available under Article 66 of the VAT Law for goods physically exported from the EU and for certain international transport and related services, subject to proof of removal from EU customs territory. For the EOR services model: (i) B2B services supplied by the Luxembourg SARL to a taxable customer established in another Member State are governed by the place-of-supply rule (customer's establishment), so Luxembourg VAT is not chargeable; the invoice must mention 'Autoliquidation - Reverse charge' and the customer's valid EU VAT ID (VIES validation). (ii) B2B services supplied to a non-EU taxable or non-taxable customer fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (zero-rated equivalent), with no Luxembourg VAT due. (iii) Staff-leasing services physically performed in Luxembourg for a foreign principal remain taxable at 17% unless the recipient demonstrates business establishment outside Luxembourg and effective use of the service in the foreign country; the supplier must hold a signed attestation of the customer's foreign establishment. (iv) Ancillary payroll and contractor-management services follow the same B2B place-of-supply analysis. The zero-rating evidence file must be completed within 90 days of the supply and kept for 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DES) lodged via the Luxembourg Single Window/ICMS with exit confirmation from the customs office of departure
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice, packing list, and proof of export weight/value
International service contract and detailed time/attendance records for EOR and payroll services
Foreign customer's VAT identification number validated via VIES (for EU customers) or an attestation of business establishment (for non-EU customers)
Bank statements and inward remittance certificates showing consideration received in the SARL's Luxembourg account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg applies no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark is used by ACD/AEDT auditors as the standard receivables substantiation window. Incorrect zero-rating or reverse-charge claims trigger reassessment within the general 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of willful VAT fraud or intentional concealment (Article 19 of the VAT Law; Section 144 AO). Clawback includes restitution of the uncollected VAT, late-payment interest accrued from the due date, and administrative fines under Article 72 of the VAT Law ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 2,500 per infraction. Where deliberate fraud is established, criminal proceedings expose the directors and the Luxembourg tax representative to imprisonment of up to 5 years and a criminal fine of up to 5 times the VAT evaded; the tax authorities may additionally hold the management company jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking prudential and conduct supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is an integral Eurozone member; both current and capital account transactions are fully liberalised under EU capital movement rules (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Article 63). There are no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or proceeds conversion. Only standard corporate tax and withholding tax withholdings apply under domestic tax law, not FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg does not impose any export proceeds surrender requirements. There is neither a statutory timeline nor a mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. All export and service proceeds remain freely convertible and transferable, subject to ordinary anti-money laundering (AML) reporting thresholds and suspicious transaction reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise (authorised as a Luxembourg payment institution or as a passport under the e-money framework) is highly viable for operational liquidity and cross-border payroll settlements, rated High. Other pan-European EMIs are acceptable for low-velocity remittance but are not recommended for capital escrow accounts nor for substantial treasury reserve buffers. Legal constraints include adherence to CSSF AML expectations, mandatory segregated client funds accounting, and a Luxembourg or EEA registered presence for the EMI; full Tier-1 bank will still be required for capital contributions and significant loan advances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg CSSF regulation requires that all beneficial owners and directors are independently identified before account opening. A physical presence for at least one director or a properly mandated authorised signatory is effectively mandatory. Remote opening is permitted only for certain banks when supported by a notarised power of attorney and a videoconference interview; most Tier-1 banks still require a face-to-face meeting at the point of UBO validation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resident in a FATF grey-listed or non-cooperative jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid tax residence certificates, three months of bank statements in source jurisdiction, legitimate source-of-wealth statement with auditor attestation, corporate real-economy contracts, and a detailed rationale for the cross-border EOR structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll throughput disproportionately high compared with capital base and staff count of the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client employment agreements, works contracts, audited payroll ledger showing consistent withholding and social declarations, accountant's confirmation letter, and cash-flow forecast evidencing that the account solely aggregates statutory wages and employer charges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party disbursements to non-resident contractors, especially in high‑risk industries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual contractor agreements, professional internal KYC file for each beneficiary, insurance policies, time-tracking records, and an automated and monitorable payroll journal; plus a written commitment to file all suspicious or large transactions in accordance with CSSF circulars.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be denominated in EUR, sent via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer) with the ISO 20022 purpose code 'SP1' (capital subscription/contribution) and with the reference 'Déclaration de souscription au capital' plus the notarised deed of incorporation. For intragroup loans, an executed intragroup loan agreement, treasury confirmation, and arm's-length interest benchmark are required. All funds are verified against the CSSF force-fraud list and correspondent banks are screened against sanctions lists.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Employee salary payments within the EEA are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with full IBAN/BIC; non-EEA contractor settlements use SWIFT MT103 (priority) or MT202 for interbank transfers; Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit are permissible for large contractual service milestones though rarely required in EOR flows. For same-day euro settlement, TARGET2 and RTGS are available through the clearing bank. Multi-currency disbursements are leveraged via correspondent banking networks, each governed by W-8BEN-E compliance or similar treaty disclosures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (maturity up to 12 months) under an ISDA/CSA Master Agreement for EUR-USD and EUR-GBP exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for high-inflation or capital-controlled jurisdictions, settled in euros against a reference rate
Cross-currency swaps for periodic commitment conversion, cleared under a standard ISDA and eligible for the commercial treasury exemption from central clearing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet and profit/loss) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and published in the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year end (if FYE 31 Dec, no later than 30 Jun)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: administrative fine EUR 250–2,000; repeated default may lead to coercive fines and court-ordered strike-off or winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (RBE) in the national UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the anniversary of the entity’s initial RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance: administrative fine up to EUR 250,000; criminal sanctions for wilful nondisclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax annual return (Model 720)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the calendar fiscal year, return due on or before 31 Dec of the following year; extensions available upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: default interest at 0.7% per month plus late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; ex officio assessment if omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the income tax return for the relevant tax year (31 Dec following the tax year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: penalty up to EUR 1,000 plus default interest on unpaid net wealth tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a réviseur d’entreprises is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the three following criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50 employees. Global EOR payroll operations typically exceed these thresholds due to high turnover and staffing volumes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LuxGAAP) in accordance with EU Accounting Directives; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for statutory accounts and mandatory for listed public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual RBE confirmation must be filed within one calendar month after the anniversary of the registration in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs. Any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be reported within one month of the transaction. The confirmed record must contain full identity data and economic interest percentages.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City, FY 2024 aggregate): 17% IRC + 7% Employment Fund surcharge on the IRC due (=1.19%) + 6.75% municipal business tax (TCC) on trade profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% IRC (plus 7% surcharge) on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profit; 50% participation exemption on qualifying dividend income; full participation exemption on substantial capital gains (>= 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price, 12-month holding period); R&D tax credit on eligible expenditures; investment tax credit for sustainable assets; net wealth tax abatement of EUR 500,000 for commercial companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 544 — annual declaration of corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune); filed electronically via the ACD eCDF portal and the myguichet.lu RTS teleprocedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory reference date: 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end for a calendar-year taxpayer. The ACD routinely grants an automatic extension to 30 June where the annual accounts have been finalised; a further conventional extension to 31 December remains requestable on formal application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS number, LEI, legal form (SARL), registered office, statutory representative and administrative contact, tax consolidation reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL files under its own RCS/LU identity. Non-resident shareholders do not enter the form; the LU director or tax representative signs and must hold a power of attorney.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reported net profit or loss before tax per the audited annual accounts (CNC Luxembourg GAAP).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the book result of the LU SARL only; intercompany EOR bills from the non-resident parent/branch must be excluded unless properly re-invoiced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: excessive remuneration, fictitious payroll, fines, gifts, expenses paid to zero-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions, and portions of interest disallowed under thin-capitalisation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the EOR staffing fee is paid to an offshore back-office, the ACD will deny deductibility absent an arm's-length service agreement and substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Section D — Participation exemption election
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the 50% exemption on dividends or the full capital-gain exemption; state qualifying shareholding percentage, acquisition price and holding period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors providing a TRC and Form 91 will be attached to the SARL's annual file to support reduced withholding under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Section E — Loss carryforward offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses against the current-year positive result; the ACD pre-fills the loss register and applies the 17-year carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign head office cannot be imputed to the LU SARL; only losses booked and recognised under Luxembourg tax law are eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Section F — Municipal business tax (TCC) base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade-income base after the EUR 175,000 abatement and apportionment to the commune of establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The EOR payroll services must be attributed to the LU commercial activity; non-resident back-office personnel do not reduce the Luxembourg TCC allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Section G — Net wealth tax (ISF) declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable wealth at the balance sheet date; deduction of the EUR 500,000 abatement and the 0.5% rate applied to the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not file ISF personally; the SARL files and pays, and may benefit from the minimum-tax regime on commencement of business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing causes an automatic provisional assessment (taxation d'office), a late-declaration surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, penalty interest of 0.6% per month on the outstanding balance, and, for repeated refusal to file, an administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000 and loss of the right to claim tax losses.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (Art. 104 LIR) on Luxembourg-source dividends paid by an SARL; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying parent holding at least 10% capital or a EUR 1.2 million acquisition price for an uninterrupted 12-month period; DTA rates typically range from 0% to 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority and execute ACD Form 91 before the payment date. The Luxembourg paying entity transmits the completed request to the ACD for an advance ruling on the applicable treaty rate; if no decision is issued before the distribution, the Luxembourg payer must withhold 15%, and the beneficial owner may claim a refund via a reduced-rate certificate or within the statutory filing window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Luxembourg WHT on interest payable to non-resident corporate lenders is 0% for professional debts (Art. 147 LIR); royalties paid to non-residents are generally not subject to Luxembourg-source WHT. EU Interest & Royalties Directive (Directive 2003/49/EC) confirms 0% WHT on qualifying connected-company payments within the EU. Under many Luxembourg DTAs (e.g., US, UK), treaty rates on interest and royalties are likewise 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No written statutory de minimis; ACD administrative guidance requires a contemporaneous Luxembourg Local File where annual intercompany transactions with a single associated enterprise exceed EUR 100,000, and a Master File where the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but enforces an equivalent minimum-substance doctrine through Art. 56 LIR, the general anti-abuse rule, and case law (Eqiom). A Global EOR staffing SARL must maintain a real physical office, resident executive director(s) with actual decision-making autonomy, local payroll records, and an operational staffing function; otherwise the ACD may recharacterise the SARL as a transparent conduit, reallocate profit to the foreign parent and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Fictitious EOR Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately issuing or booking false intercompany invoices, inflating payroll headcounts, or claiming deductions for services never rendered in order to shift profit out of Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraud penalty of 50% of the evaded tax (increased to 75% for premeditated fraud), late-interest of 0.6% per month, additional 7% Employment Fund surcharge on the penalty, and criminal fine of up to EUR 100,000 with imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years under the Luxembourg General Tax Law and Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; courts may impose a travel ban, asset freeze, disqualification from management functions and confiscation of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SARL as a mere invoicing shell with no loyalty to Luxembourg: no premises, no local payroll, no controlling staff, and all decision-making conducted by a non-resident parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and reallocation of profits to the foreign parent; denial of participation-exemption benefits and treaty relief; 50% supplementary tax on hidden distributions; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; DAC6 disclosure penalties for reportable cross-border arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The sole/signing manager may be held personally liable for the tax shortfall in insolvency-style proceedings (Art. 495, Luxembourg Commercial Code), can be barred from acting as a director for up to 10 years, and may be subject to a cross-border travel ban pending recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and retain a contemporaneous Local File and, where applicable, Master File reflecting the arm's-length return of the Luxembourg EOR entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of EUR 50,000 for failure to deliver the TP documentation on demand; the tax authority may re-impute an arm's-length margin with a 20% to 50% penalty surcharge on the adjustment, plus enforcement interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who certified the tax return is jointly assessed for the re-assessed corporate tax, and, where the failure is intentional, may face criminal sanctions and disqualification from professional office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-registration of ultimate beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), failure to conduct customer due diligence on global contractors, or unexplained cross-border salary disbursements through the EOR rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF and judicial fines of up to EUR 5 million or twice the AML benefit; daily default penalties for office renovation of the RBE; withdrawal of the professional licence of the EOR operator; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for money-laundering concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for laundering proceeds or financing anonymity structures; sanctions include custodial sentence, a multi-year travel ban, and personal restitution of all criminally derived benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying cross-border contractors as Luxembourg employees solely to claim deductions, or failing to register with Luxembourg social security (CNS, CCSS) and to withhold salary tax on actual Luxembourg payroll.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge equal to 10% of un-withheld wage tax plus 0.6% monthly interest; social security fraud penalty of up to 150% of evaded contributions; refusal to recognise foreign payroll rebilling as deductible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid salary withholding and social contributions; attachment of personal bank accounts and assets, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years for repeated payroll fraud.
